You should try the following : check your connection, disable ad-blocker, clear your browser cache, try in private mode, try from another browser/computer/connection. 0 Hegemony: Lead Your Class to Victory The Nation is in disarray and a war is waging between the classes. The working class faces a dismantled welfare system, the capitalists are losing their hard-earned profits, the middle class is gradually fading and the state is sinking into a deep deficit. Amidst all this chaos, the only person who can provide guidance is... you. Will you take the side of the working class and fight for social reforms? Or will you stand with the corporations and the free market? Will you help the government try to keep it all together, or will you try to enforce your agenda no matter the cost to the country? Hegemony is an asymmetric politico-economic card-driven board game for 2-4 players that puts you in the role of one of the socio-economic groups in a fictional state: The Working Class, the Middle Class, the Capitalist Class and the State itself. Number of players: 2 - 4 Game duration: 98 mn Complexity: 4 / 5 Play Hegemony: Lead Your Class to Victory and 1414 other games online. No download necessary - play directly from your web browser. With your friends and thousands of players from the whole world. Free. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Action Phase 2 Common Actions 3 Working Class 3.1 Basic Actions 3.2 Free Actions 4 Middle Class 4.1 Basic Actions 4.2 Free Actions 5 Capitalist Class 5.1 Basic Actions 5.2 Free Actions 6 State 6.1 Basic Actions 6.2 Free Actions Action Phase During the action phase, players take actions in turn, in increasing status order (Working Class, Middle Class, Capitalist Class, State). Every time it’s your turn, you must play a card. For your Main Action , you may take either the action on the card or a Basic Action of your choice as listed in the next section. If you cannot take the action on the card, you may still use the card for a Basic Action. As well as the basic action, you may take a single Free Action in your turn. This can be before or after your Main Action, but it cannot be in the middle. You cannot pass. There should be no reason to, as basic actions such as Apply Political Pressure are always of benefit to you. The action phase continues until each player has taken 5 actions. This should mean they have 2 cards remaining in their hand. The table below summarises the basic and free actions available to each class. Common Actions Every class has a common basic action: Propose a Bill: You take one Bill marker and place it on a desired, adjacent policy section where do not already have a marker. You may also spend 1 Influence to call an Immediate Vote for the proposed Bill. Every class has a common free action: Paying Off Loan: You spend 50 Vardis (50 money) to discard a Loan. Working Class Basic Actions Apply Political Pressure: You may add 3 voting cubes to the Bag. Assign Workers: You can choose up to 3 of your non-committed Workers from anywhere on the board, place them in available Companies, and commit them. Buy Resources (Goods & Services): You can choose a single good or service and buy from up to two sources as many tokens as your current population per source. Strike: You can place a Strike token on up to two Companies, which prevents them from producing. Demonstration: You can place a Demonstration token in the Unemployed Workers area if the number of unemployed workers is at least 2 higher than available Working Class worker slots. Free Actions Claim Benefits: You can receive the benefits that the State has placed in the appropriate State Benefits boxes. Swap Workers: You may swap any number of a skilled worker with an unskilled worker without affecting their commitment in Companies. Spend Healthcare equal to population, to gain 1 Prosperity, gain VP according to prosperity track slot and extra 2VP, then received an unskilled worker in the Unemployed Worker area. Spend Education equal to population, to gain 1 Prosperity, gain VP according to prosperity track slot, then Upgrade one of your unskilled workers anywhere on the board to a skilled one. I also don't fully believe in the Class Conflict, especially not as a fixed inescapable truth.  I like the card-driven play (play a card for effect or discard for basic action) and that the cards have a slight 'epic event feel'. [Rating: 1/10] Well done simulation of Capitalism. Not a board game, because no room for decisions, 5 turn long pre-destined and random card trigger game.  CAUTION! This game is just overhyped at this moment. If the hype upvoters are done, the real value of the game will drop to around 40$ and have a score of 6.9-7.2. Only recommended for Finance and Economist students.

[Rating: 1/10] Note due au travail de localisationde Don't Panic Games... ou plutôt l'absence de travail, le nombres d'erreurs qui impactent le jeu est assez colossale... Ce que je peux tolérer, projet trop ambitieux pour l'éditeur -à la limite- mais l'absence de communication alors que présents sur un fil dédié à ces erratas... non.   Sinon pour le jeu c'est un solide 9/10:  De ces jeux qu'on éspère pouvoir sortir régulièrment, malgré la lourdeur du monstre.  Très didactique et globalement cohérent, avec Twillight Struggle ou Gigawatt des jeux superbes même en temps qu'outils de connaissances et compréhensi

[Rating: 1/10] Erreurs sur la VF qui rendent le jeu injouable. L'éditeur a décidé de proposer un pack de correction payant en septembre ! Honteux.

[Rating: 1/10] Fun to play once or twice. It's long due to how much bloat it has. Very good at feeling like an economy sim and less like a game with economy in it. Play once or twice then it's done.  Update: Played a third time on BGA. This is not a game for me. Its well made and the mechanisms and simulation are genuinely fun, but the time it takes to actually get through everything is insane. If anyone in your group has AP then steer clear.   Update 2: I have been roped into a fourth time. This is not even a game. I just did a bunch of random junk and won. Its also heavily dependant on what cards you draw.

[Rating: 1/10] Another asymmetric euro game where everybody's too tired to look at the other boards, too exhausted to talk. So nothing interesting happens.
